review_notes: I skimmed the whole file for repeated blocks. I read the candidate declarations in full and confirmed their line numbers with Read and Grep. Only the four findings below are evidenced. Smaller repetitions were skipped as too short, or as duplicated branches inside one proof. Examples are the two branches of `exists_uniform_inner_supportBall`, the `|t * v p| ≤ |t| * bound` calculations in the target-geodesic section, and the two `exp`-shift partition computations. The rewrites are sketches that I have not compiled. I did not check every call site. Coverage is marked partial because the more than 8,000 lines of this file were not each read line by line.

findings.problem: `interior_gap` and `interior_sum_abs_gap` (lines 458–491) have the same hypotheses and almost the same proof. Both choose a ball around `u` inside `K`, test the point `u + (r/2) • signVector x`, and rewrite with `pairing_add_left`, `pairing_smul_left` and `pairing_signVector`. The only difference is the last step. `interior_gap` finishes with `norm_le_sum_abs`, so it is the weaker `‖x‖` form of the sharper `∑ |x i|` statement. The ball/sign-vector argument is therefore written twice.
findings.proposed_change: Prove only the sharper statement, with `δ * ∑ i, |x i|`, inside `SupportFunction`. Define `interior_gap` from it by multiplying `norm_le_sum_abs x` by `hδ.le`. The statement is `∃ δ > 0, ∀ x, δ * ∑ i, |x i| ≤ supportFunction K x - pairing u x`. Delete the body at lines 465–491 and have `MonomialIntegrability.interior_sum_abs_gap` be a one-line alias of the new lemma, or update its callers (`integrable_monomialWeight_of_support_le`, `exists_phase_le_const_sub_mul_sum_abs`). The derived lemma would read: `obtain ⟨δ, hδ, h⟩ := interior_sum_abs_gap hcompact hu; exact ⟨δ, hδ, fun x => (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (norm_le_sum_abs x) hδ.le).trans (h x)⟩`. `norm_le_sum_abs` is already in `SupportFunction`, so nothing moves across namespaces.
findings.benefit: Removes about 25 lines of duplicated geometric reasoning. The two gap estimates can no longer drift apart. A reader sees at once that the norm version is a corollary of the coordinatewise-sum version.

findings.problem: The mollification of the support function (lines 1787–1885) is redone verbatim for `sourceSupportClipping F R` (lines 6679–7007). The same four steps are repeated. (1) Rewrite the convolution as `∫ ρ.normed t * f (x - t)`. (2) Apply `integral_convexOn_of_integrand_ae`, with the translate-and-smul convexity step and the `convolutionExists_left` integrability step. (3) Bound `dist` via `ρ.dist_normed_convolution_le` plus a Lipschitz estimate and a `Real.coe_toNNReal` cast. (4) Pick the bump with `δ := ε/(L+1)`, `⟨δ/2, δ, _, _⟩`, and prove `L*δ < ε` by `div_lt_iff₀; nlinarith`. These steps use nothing about the support function or the clipping beyond continuity, convexity and a Lipschitz constant. `convexOn_mollifiedSourceSupportClipping` (6690–6724) is an exact copy of `convexOn_mollifiedSupport`, and the `hsmall`/`ρ` blocks at 1866–1885 and 6987–7007 are identical.
findings.proposed_change: Add a generic lemma section. (a) For `f : Space n → ℝ` with `Continuous f` and `ConvexOn ℝ univ f`, and any `ρ : ContDiffBump 0`, the map `ρ.normed volume ⋆ f` is `ContDiff ℝ ∞` and `ConvexOn ℝ univ`. (b) If `LipschitzWith L f` then `dist ((ρ.normed volume ⋆ f) x) (f x) ≤ L * ρ.rOut`. (c) For `L ≥ 0` and `ε > 0` there is a `ρ : ContDiffBump 0` with `L * ρ.rOut < ε`, taking `δ = ε/(L+1)` as at 1869–1872. Proof of (a): move the existing proofs of `contDiff_mollifiedSupport` and `convexOn_mollifiedSupport` verbatim, replacing `supportFunction K` by `f`. Proof of (b): reuse `dist_mollifiedSupport_le` with `hlip.dist_le_mul y x` and `ball`. Rewrite `exists_smooth_convex_potential_uniformly_close` by instantiating with `f := supportFunction K`, `L := (n*R : ℝ≥0)`, using `supportFunction_lipschitzWith`. Rewrite `exists_smooth_sourceSupportClipping_recovery` and `mollifiedSourceSupportClipping_supportBound` with `f := sourceSupportClipping F R` and `L := sourceBodyLipschitzConstant K`, using `sourceSupportClipping_lipschitz`. The existing `hcoe` casts then disappear because the lemma is stated with an `NNReal` Lipschitz constant.
findings.benefit: About 120 lines are replaced by one generic lemma and two short instantiations. A future change to the mollifier, such as a different regularisation, is made once. The convex-mollification argument is isolated and reviewable. It also keeps the support-function material (`contDiff_…`, `convexOn_…`) from being cloned for every new convex Lipschitz function.

findings.problem: Four proofs repeat the same chain: for `‖p‖ ≤ R`, `pairing p x - pairing p y = pairing p (x - y) ≤ |…| ≤ (n*‖p‖)*‖x-y‖ ≤ (n*R)*dist x y`. Each rederives it from `abs_pairing_le_dimension_mul_norm` with a `le_abs_self`/`mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_*`/`dist_eq_norm` calculation. The sites are `supportFunction_lipschitzWith` (1715–1729), `convex_supportCompatible_lipschitz` (2455–2468), `phase_abs_sub_le` (2518–2542), and `finiteEnergyTargetGeodesic_lipschitz` (7787–7813). The last two also redo `pairing_sub_right` inline by `simp only [SupportFunction.pairing, Pi.sub_apply, mul_sub, Finset.sum_sub_distrib]`, although `pairing_sub_right` already exists in `ArbitraryBodySmoothConvexPotentialBridge`.
findings.proposed_change: After `abs_pairing_le_dimension_mul_norm` in `MonomialDivergence`, add `pairing_sub_sub_le {p : Space n} {R : ℝ} (hp : ‖p‖ ≤ R) (x y) : |pairing p x - pairing p y| ≤ ((n:ℝ)*R) * dist x y`. Prove it via `pairing_sub_right` (moved up beside `pairing_sub_left`), then `abs_pairing_le_dimension_mul_norm p (x - y)`, then `mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hp (Nat.cast_nonneg n)) (norm_nonneg _)` and `dist_eq_norm`. Rewrites: `hpair` at 1715–1729 becomes `(le_abs_self _).trans (pairing_sub_sub_le (hR u hu) x y)` after `pairing_sub_right`; `hsupport` at 2455–2468 becomes `rw [hmax]; exact (le_abs_self _).trans (by simpa [pairing_sub_right] using pairing_sub_sub_le (norm_le_bodyRadius K u hu) (x - y) 0)` or a similar `pairing_sub_sub_le` application. For `phase_abs_sub_le` the `hpair` is exactly `pairing_sub_sub_le (monomialExponent_norm_le_bodyRadius K u) x y`. For `finiteEnergyTargetGeodesic_lipschitz` the `hpair` is `(le_abs_self _).trans (pairing_sub_sub_le (norm_le_bodyRadius K p hp.1) x y)`. Each of the four sites shrinks from 10–25 lines to one or two.
findings.benefit: Four near-identical calculation chains collapse into one named inequality. The Lipschitz proofs now state their real content: the support function, the Legendre transform, and the phase are Lipschitz because `|pairing p ·|` is. The mixed `‖x-y‖`/`dist` bookkeeping and the repeated inline `pairing` expansion are done once.

findings.problem: Two roughly 100-line proofs (lines 5676–5781 and 8041–8139) are the same ball-averaging argument. Both fix `x` and take the ball `Metric.ball c (ρ/2) ⊆ K` with `δ‖x‖ ≤ pairing p x` on it. Both integrate `δ‖x‖ − g x ≤ pairing p x − g x ≤ G p` over the ball, with the constant integral equal to `ρ^n·(…)`. Both enlarge from the ball to `K.carrier` using `setIntegral_mono_set` and nonnegativity of `G`. Both convert `∫_K G = vol(K)·energy` and divide by `ρ^n` via `le_div_iff₀`, finishing with `ring`. They differ only in the instantiation. In one, `g` is `minimumNormalizedSourceContinuousMap D` and `G` is `minimumNormalizedSourceBodyDual D`. In the other, `g` is `F.potential` and `G` is `(sourceExtendedBodyLegendre F.potential p).toReal`. The pointwise Fenchel inequality is a hypothesis in each case.
findings.proposed_change: Prove one lemma next to `exists_uniform_inner_supportBall`. For `K : CenteredBody n`, `g G : Space n → ℝ`, and `hG : IntegrableOn G K.carrier volume`, assume `0 ≤ᵐ[volume.restrict K.carrier] G` and `∀ᵐ p ∂(volume.restrict K.carrier), ∀ x, pairing p x - g x ≤ G p`. The conclusion is `∃ δ B, 0 < δ ∧ 0 < B ∧ ∀ x, δ * ‖x‖ ≤ g x + B * ((normalizedVolume K.carrier)⁻¹ * ∫ p in K.carrier, G p)`. The proof is the existing one. Obtain `ρ δ` from `exists_uniform_inner_supportBall`, set `B := normalizedVolume K / ρ^n`, and run the ball integral chain (`setIntegral_const`, `realVolume_uniformInnerBall`, `setIntegral_mono_on`/`integral_mono_ae`, `setIntegral_mono_set`) once. Then `exists_minimumNormalizedSource_linear_coercivity` becomes the lemma instantiated at `G := minimumNormalizedSourceBodyDual D`. It uses `minimumNormalizedSourceBodyFenchel_le`, `minimumNormalizedSourceBodyDual_integrableOn` and `minimumNormalizedSourceBodyDual_nonneg` as hypotheses, then `minimumNormalizedSourceBodyDual_energy` to rewrite the energy term. `exists_finiteEnergySource_linear_coercivity` becomes the lemma instantiated at `G := fun p => (sourceExtendedBodyLegendre F.potential p).toReal`. It uses `finiteEnergyFiniteTarget_fenchel` on `ae_mem_finiteEnergyFiniteTargetSet F`, `finiteEnergySourceExtendedLegendre_integrableOn`, `ENNReal.toReal_nonneg` and `finiteEnergySourceBodyEnergy_eq_setIntegral`. The a.e. form of the Fenchel hypothesis covers both, since the first caller's pointwise version implies it.
findings.benefit: One shared coercivity lemma replaces about 200 lines of parallel proof, and the two callers become about 15 lines each. Any later repair to the uniform-ball constants affects one place. The common structure becomes visible: both coercivity bounds are the same mass estimate with different dual integrands.
